#flang is a constructed language the user is building; its grammar rules are defined iteratively in conversation and updated when the user requests changes.
#flang noun cases: accusative adds "-a" (fash → fasha), genitive adds "-i" (fash → fashi), instrumental adds "-u" (fash → fashu).
#flang verbs take the same case endings as nouns: accusative "-a" (fala → falaa), genitive "-i" (fala → falai), instrumental "-u" (fala → falau).

#flang articles precede the noun: definite article is "fi", indefinite article is "fa" (e.g. "fi fash" = the house, "fa fash" = a house). The definite article was changed from "f" to "fi" at the user's request.
#flang past tense is formed by adding "-o" to the verb base: "fala" (to walk) → "falo"; "fika" (eats) → "fiko" (ate).
#flang vocabulary: flom = dog, fash = house, fol = cat, fona = woman, fala = to walk, fik- = to eat.
#flang genitive word order puts the possessor first and the possessed noun last, and only the possessor takes "-i": "flomi fash" = the dog's house, "fashi flom" = the house's dog.
#flang example translations: "Fi flom fika fa fol" = the dog eats a cat; "Fi flom fiko fa fol" = the dog ate a cat; "Fi fona fiko fa fol" = the woman ate a cat.

On 2023/05/25 the user asked about the differences between symptoms of multiple sclerosis (MS) and Parkinson's disease (PD), then about their causes and promising new treatments. #multiple_sclerosis #parkinsons_disease
MS is a chronic autoimmune disease of the central nervous system where the immune system attacks myelin, the protective covering of nerve fibers. #multiple_sclerosis

Common MS symptoms: vision problems (blurred/double vision, color vision loss, eye pain), motor problems (weakness, spasticity, tremor, poor coordination/balance), sensory problems (numbness, tingling, burning, pain), disabling fatigue not relieved by rest, cognitive issues (memory, attention, problem-solving), and emotional issues (depression, anxiety, mood swings). #multiple_sclerosis
Parkinson's disease is a neurodegenerative disorder of the motor system caused by progressive loss of dopamine-producing neurons in the brain. #parkinsons_disease

Classic PD symptoms: resting tremor (often first symptom, typically one hand/arm), rigidity, bradykinesia (slowness of movement), postural instability and falls, plus non-motor symptoms like depression, anxiety, constipation, sleep disorders and cognitive impairment. #parkinsons_disease

Common MS symptoms: vision problems (blurred or double vision, loss of color vision, pain behind the eyes) and motor problems (weakness, spasticity, tremor, poor coordination and balance). #multiple_sclerosis

MS also causes sensory symptoms (numbness, tingling, burning, pain), disabling fatigue not relieved by rest, cognitive problems (memory, attention, problem-solving), and emotional problems (depression, anxiety, mood swings). #multiple_sclerosis

MS is believed to arise from a combination of genetic, environmental and immune factors; risk factors mentioned include certain predisposing genes, viral infections, toxins, smoking, low vitamin D and obesity. #multiple_sclerosis

PD is thought to result from genetic and environmental factors plus accumulation of abnormal proteins (alpha-synuclein and tau); risk factors mentioned include pesticides, head injuries and certain medications. #parkinsons_disease

Promising MS treatments: disease-modifying therapies such as ocrelizumab (anti-B-cell antibody; reduces relapses in relapsing-remitting MS, slows disability in primary progressive MS) and siponimod (S1P receptor modulator for secondary progressive MS), plus investigational stem cell therapy. #multiple_sclerosis

Promising PD treatments: gene therapy such as GDNF gene delivery to the brain (improved dopamine and motor function in preclinical studies) and focused ultrasound that temporarily opens the blood-brain barrier to allow targeted drug delivery; both were still early-stage as of 2023. #parkinsons_disease

Promising MS treatments include disease-modifying therapies such as ocrelizumab (anti-B-cell antibody; reduces relapses in relapsing-remitting MS and slows disability in primary progressive MS) and siponimod (S1P receptor modulator for secondary progressive MS). #multiple_sclerosis
Stem cell therapy is being investigated for MS, with early studies showing reduced disease activity and disability progression. #multiple_sclerosis

Key distinction between MS and PD: MS causes varied neurological symptoms that can differ in intensity and body location, while PD mainly affects the motor system with movement symptoms that worsen over time; PD typically affects older adults, whereas MS can affect people of any age. #multiple_sclerosis #parkinsons_disease
